e.title: **按「执业领域」把开源精算工具排成一份指南，并说明它与「组织清单」页的差别**：一份提交给北美财险精算学会官网的**未合并提案**逐字写着「**它回答的问题与 Projects 页不同。**Projects 是**本组织的库存清单，**每天从 GitHub API 刷新，**并且保持原样**。**而 Field Guide 从问题出发：**准备金、尾部拟合、可信度、资本」**；**实测其数据文件为 **63 行工具 × 20 个领域****，**由一份 CSV 生成页面**（**逐字「让发布的页面与源数据保持同步」**），**并带语言筛选**
e.title_en: Ordering open-source actuarial tools into a guide by area of practice, and stating how it differs from the organisation inventory page: an unmerged proposal submitted to the North American casualty actuarial society website states verbatim that it answers a different question than the projects page, which is the organisation inventory refreshed daily from the interface and which stays exactly as it is, whereas the field guide starts from the problem, reserving, tail fitting, credibility, capital — measured at sixty-three tool rows across twenty areas, rendered from a CSV so that the published page stays in sync with the source data, with language filtering
e.title_hk: **按「執業領域」把開源精算工具排成一份指南，並說明它與「組織清單」頁的差別**：一份提交給北美財險精算學會官網的**未合併提案**逐字寫著「**它回答的問題與 Projects 頁不同。**Projects 是**本組織的庫存清單，每天從 GitHub API 刷新，並且保持原樣**。**而 Field Guide 從問題出發：**準備金、尾部擬合、可信度、資本」**；**實測其數據文件為 **63 行工具 × 20 個領域****，**由一份 CSV 生成頁面**（**逐字「讓發布的頁面與源數據保持同步」**），**並帶語言篩選**
e.summary: 一份**按执业领域组织的开源精算工具指南**（**提交给北美财险精算学会官网的提案**，★0、Python、**未合并**）：**逐字自述其组织维度为**「**按执业领域分组的开源精算工具集**，**覆盖该学会组织以及更广的 R、Python 与 Julia 生态」**；**其最值得记的一处是它**把自己的组织维度与另一页面对照说清****——**逐字「**它回答的问题与 Projects 页不同。**Projects 是该组织的**库存清单**，**每天从 GitHub API 刷新，**并且保持原样**。**而 Field Guide **从问题出发**：**准备金、尾部拟合、可信度、资本**」**；**第二处是它**由一份 CSV 生成**——**逐字说明有一个脚本「**从一份 CSV 数据文件渲染这份指南，**使发布的页面与源数据保持同步」**；**第三处是它**把语言与来源做成可筛的字段****（**CSV 列为 `area, tool, url, repo_url, language, cas_hosted, description`**；**前端加上**按语言与主办组织筛选的交互**）；**⭐ 本词条另做了一次**外部清单对本池的对照****：**该 CSV 的 **63 件工具里有 17 件**在本站池／wiki 中未找到**（**其中绝大多数是**该学会自己托管、**而最后推送**落在窗口之外的仓库**）
e.summary_hk: 一份**按執業領域組織的開源精算工具指南**（**提交給北美財險精算學會官網的提案**，★0、Python、**未合併**）：**逐字自述其組織維度為**「**按執業領域分組的開源精算工具集**，**覆蓋該學會組織以及更廣的 R、Python 與 Julia 生態」**；**其最值得記的一處是它**把自己的組織維度與另一頁面對照說清****——**逐字「**它回答的問題與 Projects 頁不同。**Projects 是該組織的**庫存清單**，**每天從 GitHub API 刷新，並且保持原樣**。**而 Field Guide **從問題出發**：**準備金、尾部擬合、可信度、資本**」**；**第二處是它**由一份 CSV 生成**——**逐字說明有一個腳本「**從一份 CSV 數據文件渲染這份指南，**使發布的頁面與源數據保持同步」**；**第三處是它**把語言與來源做成可篩的字段****（**CSV 列為 `area, tool, url, repo_url, language, cas_hosted, description`**；**前端加上**按語言與主辦組織篩選的交互**）；**⭐ 本詞條另做了一次**外部清單對本池的對照****：**該 CSV 的 63 件工具裡有 **17 件**在本站池／wiki 中未找到**（**其中絕大多數是**該學會自己託管、**而最後推送**落在窗口之外的倉庫**）
e.summary_en: A guide to open-source actuarial tools organised by area of practice, submitted as a proposal to the North American casualty actuarial society website — 0 stars, Python, unmerged — describing itself verbatim as the open-source actuarial toolset grouped by area of practice and covering the society organisation alongside the wider R, Python and Julia ecosystems. **Its most notable feature is that it states how its organising dimension differs from another page**: verbatim, it answers a different question than the projects page, which is the organisation inventory refreshed daily from the interface and which stays exactly as it is, whereas the guide starts from the problem, reserving, tail fitting, credibility and capital. **The second is that it is generated from a CSV**, the repository stating verbatim that a script renders the guide from a data file so that the published page stays in sync with the source data. **The third is that language and hosting are filterable fields**, the data file carrying area, tool, URL, repository URL, language, whether the society hosts it, and a description, with client-side filtering by language and organisation. ⭐ **This entry also ran an external cross-check**: seventeen of the sixty-three tools in that data file were not found in this site’s pool or wiki, most of them repositories hosted by the society itself whose last push falls outside the window.
e.body:
**cas-field-guide**（仓库与提案：`casact/casact.github.io` 上的一号拉取请求，**来自 `philobishay` 的分支**）**是一份按执业领域组织的开源精算工具指南**：**逐字自述为**「**A Field Guide page: the open-source actuarial toolset grouped by area of practice, covering the casact organization alongside the wider R, Python, and Julia ecosystems. 63 listings under 20 headings, from Reserving through Indexes and task views.**」**。**实测**：**提案状态为**开启且未合并****（**该仓库与上游同名仓库的一号拉取请求均如此**）；**改动规模为 **10 个文件、878 行新增、2 行删除****；**其数据文件实测为 **63 行工具（＋表头共 64 行）× **20 个领域****（**经 raw 实测并逐行读入统计**）。**⭐ 一处**窗口证据**值得先写**：**`casact` 组织实测共 **46 个仓库**，**而**在窗口内（推送晚于 2026-09-05）的**只有 2 个****——**`chainladder-python`（279★，**已在池内**）与本提案的目标仓库 `casact/casact.github.io`（**0★、Python、2,746 KB、**创建 2026-07-13、**最后推送 2026-09-10**）**（**均 GitHub API 实测值**）**。本条目属于本轮主题**「源与生成物」**；**⭐⭐⭐ 它是本轮四条里**唯一一条**把「组织维度」本身当成要说明的事**的****。

可核实信息（**均拉取请求正文、CSV、trend**与仓库 API 实测**）：⭐⭐⭐ **① 它把自己的组织维度与**另一个页面**对照说清**——**上游提案正文逐字为**：**「**It answers a different question than the Projects page. Projects is the org**（原文此处撇号为 ASCII U+0027，本词条按站内既有约定写作 U+2019）**s inventory, refreshed daily from the GitHub API, and it stays exactly as it is. The Field Guide starts from the problem instead: reserving, tail fitting, credibility, capital. Both pages now cross-link so a reader lands on the right one.**」**⭐⭐⭐ **四处值得记**：**① ⭐⭐⭐ **「库存清单」与「从问题出发」是两种**组织维度****——**⭐ 即**同一批工具**按**来源**排和按**要解决的问题**排，**得到两份不同的东西****（**⭐ 本词条认为这是本站所收条目里**把「分类维度」讲得最直白的一处**：**它没有说「我们的清单更好」，**而是说**两者回答不同的问题****）；**② ⭐⭐⭐ **旧页面的**自动刷新方式**被写明**（**逐字「每天从 GitHub API 刷新」**）**——**⭐ 即**读者知道**那一页为什么「保持原样」****；**③ ⭐⭐⭐ **新页面给出**四个问题域作为例子****（**准备金／尾部拟合／可信度／资本**）**——**⭐ 即**「从问题出发」**不是口号，**而有了**具体的第一层分组****；**④ ⭐⭐ **两页**互相链接**（**逐字「这样读者会落到对的那一页」**）**——**⭐ 即**两种组织方式**被设计成共存，**而不是替换****。**② ⭐⭐⭐ **它由一份 CSV 生成，且这一点被逐字说明**——**提案正文逐字为**：**「**Data-driven generation（`scripts/generate_field_guide.py`）: Python script that renders the Field Guide from a CSV data file（`docs/_data/field_guide.csv`）, **keeping the published page in sync with the source data**」**；**实测该 CSV 的列为** **`area, tool, url, repo_url, language, cas_hosted, description`**⭐⭐⭐ **四处值得记**：**① ⭐⭐⭐ **「让发布的页面与源数据保持同步」**是本条**最符合本轮主题的一句**——**⭐ 即**页面**是生成物**，**CSV 是源**；**② ⭐⭐⭐ **每一件工具**一行**，**而**行里带着**判断所需的字段****（**领域、语言、**是否该学会托管**）**——**⭐ 即**数据的形状**决定了能筛什么**；**③ ⭐⭐ **`cas_hosted` 是一个**布尔字段**（**实测取值 `yes`／`no`**）**——**⭐ 即**「谁托管」被当成**一等维度**，**而不是留给读者去查**；**④ ⭐⭐ **实测 20 个领域的人数差别很大**（**准备金 8、**模拟与合成理赔 6、**可信度与经验费率 5、**频率—案均定价 4、**死亡率与生命或然 4、**数据标准与数据集 4、**损失分布 3、**尾部与极值 3、**聚合损失建模 3、**机器学习与文本 3、**学习与第一次贡献 3、**索引与任务视图 3，**其余各 1–2**）**——**⭐ 即**这份清单**本身就透露了**该生态的密度**（**准备金最密，**而**资本建模只有 1**）**。**③ ⭐⭐⭐ **它把「语言」与「主办组织」做成可筛的交互**——**提案正文逐字说明前端脚本加上**「**与该站配色一致的**语言指示圆点（**与 GitHub 的语言着色一致）、**筛选标签（**筛选 chips）**」**⭐⭐ **三处值得记**：**① ⭐⭐ **颜色与 GitHub 的 linguist 配色一致**——**⭐ 即**读者**不需要学一套新颜色**；**② ⭐⭐ **筛选在客户端**（**静态页面 + JS**）**——**⭐ 即**不需要后端**（**⭐ 与 [[ducklm-sql-glm]] 的「不需要扩展、不需要驱动」属同一取向：**把依赖减到最少**）；**③ ⭐⭐ **按**语言**与**主办组织**两个维度筛**——**⭐ 即**它把**两条最常用的检索路径**直接做成了交互**。**④ ⭐⭐⭐ **本词条用它做了一次**外部清单对照**（这是本轮的方法，也是本条的附加价值）**：**把该 CSV 的 63 件工具**逐件与本站池（1241 条）与 wiki（1131 条）的 `source`／`title`／slug 对照**后，**有 **17 件未找到****——**其中绝大多数**是**该学会自己托管（`cas_hosted: yes`）而**最后推送落在窗口之外**的仓库**（**如 `casact/SEAT`、`casact/linearscore`、`casact/casdown`、`casact/consumer_vehicle_toolkit`、`casact/stan_stans`、`casact/painless_glms`、`casact/GAM_Examples`、`casact/Anonymizing-Ratemaking-Datasets-using-GANs`、`casact/CAS-Project-Health-Insurance-Fraud-Detection`、`casact/covid_19_data`、`casact/pres_higher_learning`、`casact/catastrophe-loss-prediction-with-NLP`、`casact/pull_request_tutorial`、`casact/OSSCIntro`**）**⭐⭐⭐ **三处值得记**：**① ⭐⭐⭐ **这份清单因此是一份**由外部来源给出的、可核对的缺口清单****——**⭐ 本词条认为这是本轮最有价值的一次方法收获**：**与其继续猜关键词，**不如拿一份别人编好的目录来**照自己的池子****；**② ⭐⭐⭐ **而对照结果同时说明**缺口不在「有没有人做」，**而在**「窗口内有没有人推送」****——**⭐ 即**这些仓库**多数已存在多年**，**只是**不在窗口内活动**（**⭐ 故本轮**不因其存在而收录**，**而是**把这份清单记为**待核清单**）；**③ ⭐⭐ **⭐ 本词条亦如实说明该对照是**粗糙匹配**（**按字符串包含与 slug 化比较**）**，**故**17 这个数**可能包含**本已收录但命名不同者**（**⚠️ 未逐件人工复核**）。**⑤ ⭐ 其余可核实细节**：**① **该提案是**由一位外部贡献者提出的**（**其分支与上游同名仓库的一号拉取请求**）**——**⭐ 即**一份专业团体的公开目录**可以由**外部人补上**；**② **其数据文件里**「死亡率与生命或然」等**领域归组**与我们自己的类目**是两套不同的切法**（**⭐ 本词条**不主张**哪一套更好，**因为**未做比较**）；**③ **其正文逐字把**「索引与任务视图」**也列为一类**（**⭐ 即**它把「别人的索引」**也当成一类工具**）**。**⑥ ⭐⭐ 可与本站条目并读**：[[cran-actuarial-task-view]]、[[chainladder-python]]、[[haute]]、[[insurancerating]]、[[lossmodels]]、[[reservingmodels]]。

⚠️ **如实标注**：**① ⚠️⚠️ **四处**未合并且无许可****：**该提案**未合并**（**本词条实测其状态为 open**）**，**故**它不是该学会已发布的页面**——**⭐ 本词条**据此**只把它记为**一份提案与一份数据文件**，**不主张**它已上线或被采纳**；**且**目标仓库与分支仓库的根目录 `LICENSE`／`LICENSE.md` 探测**均为 HTTP 404**（**GitHub 许可字段为空**）**——**⭐ 而**其中**列出的 63 件工具**各有自己的许可**（**⭐ 本词条**未逐件核对**）。**② ⚠️⚠️ **本次**没有打开其任何页面或运行其任何脚本****——**未运行 `generate_field_guide.py`、未打开其静态页面或 JS、未跑其任何检查**；**故**本词条**不主张**该页面可渲染、其筛选可用、或其后端生成过程如其所述**——**⭐ 本词条**实际做的是**把 CSV 逐行读入并统计**（**63 行、20 领域、7 列**）**，**以及**把 63 件工具与本站池做字符串级对照**。**③ ⚠️⚠️ **未核实**该指南的收录标准**（**⭐ 即**未核对**它是按什么取舍的、**是否**遗漏了明显该收的东西**）——**⭐ 这是本条目**最需要后续核实的一处**。**④ ⭐ ⚠️ **一处**计数差异**如实记录**：**分支上的提案正文逐字写**「58 tools across 20 functional areas」**，**而上游提案正文逐字写**「**63 listings under 20 headings**」**，**而**本词条**实测其数据文件为 **63 行工具****——**⭐ 本词条**据此指出**「58」这一处**与实测不符**（**⚠️ 可能的解释包括**分支正文未随数据更新、**或**两者对「工具」的计数口径不同**；**⭐ 本词条**未读该生成脚本，**故**不做判断**）。**⑤ ⚠️ **未核实**该学会是否会采纳**（**⭐ 本词条不主张任何一方立场**）。**⑥ ⚠️ **本条目所记为**2026-09-11 所见****。**核实说明**：`https://api.github.com/repos/casact/casact.github.io`、其**一号拉取请求**、其分支仓库 `philobishay/casact.github.io`**及其同名一号拉取请求**、以及**`casact` 组织仓库清单（46 个仓库）**均于 2026-09-11 经 GitHub API 实测读取；**其数据文件 `docs/_data/field_guide.csv` 经 raw 实测逐行读入（63 行工具＋表头，7 列，20 个领域）**；两个根目录的 `LICENSE`／`LICENSE.md` 存在性经 raw 探测确认（均为 HTTP 404）；**未克隆、未运行其任何脚本、未打开其任何页面、未逐件核对其所列工具的许可或收录标准、未做其他网络观察**。

page in sync with the source data**」；實測該 CSV 的列為 `area, tool, url, repo_url, language, cas_hosted, description`**四處**：**① ⭐⭐⭐「讓發布的頁面與源數據保持同步」**（**頁面是生成物，CSV 是源**）；**② 件未找到**——其中絕大多數是**該學會自己託管而最後推送落在窗口之外**的倉庫（如 e.body_en:
**cas-field-guide** (the repository and proposal being pull request number one against `casact/casact.github.io`, coming from a fork by a named contributor) **is a guide to open-source actuarial tools organised by area of practice**, describing itself verbatim as a field guide page presenting the open-source actuarial toolset grouped by area of practice, covering the society organisation alongside the wider R, Python and Julia ecosystems with sixty-three listings under twenty headings. **Measured: the proposal is open and unmerged**, both in the repository and upstream; **its size is ten changed files with eight hundred and seventy-eight additions and two deletions**; **and its data file measures sixty-three tool rows across twenty areas**, read row by row over raw. ⭐ **One window fact is worth stating first**: **the society organisation measurably holds forty-six repositories of which only two were pushed inside the window**, one being a reserving library already in this site’s pool and the other being this proposal’s target repository, a Python site repository of 2,746 KB created on 2026-07-13 and last pushed on 2026-09-10. This entry belongs to this round’s theme of **source and generated artefact**, and ⭐⭐⭐ **of the four it is the only one that makes its own organising dimension something to be explained**.

Verifiable details (**read from the proposal bodies, the data file and the repository interface**): ⭐⭐⭐ **① It states how its organising dimension differs from another page** — the upstream proposal states verbatim that it answers a different question than the projects page, **which is the organisation inventory refreshed daily from the interface and which stays exactly as it is**, whereas the field guide **starts from the problem instead: reserving, tail fitting, credibility, capital**, and that both pages now cross-link so a reader lands on the right one (the original uses an ASCII apostrophe, rendered here per site convention) ⭐⭐⭐ **Four things**: ⭐⭐⭐ **an inventory and starting from the problem are two organising dimensions**, so the same set of tools ordered by where it came from and ordered by what it is for produces two different artefacts, ⭐ **and the entry notes that it does not claim its own list is better but that the two answer different questions, which this entry takes as the plainest account of a classification dimension collected here**; ⭐⭐⭐ **how the older page refreshes itself is stated, daily from the interface, so a reader knows why that page stays as it is**; ⭐⭐⭐ **four problem areas are given as examples, reserving, tail fitting, credibility and capital, so starting from the problem is not a slogan but has a concrete first level**; **and ⭐⭐ the two pages cross-link, so the two organising methods are designed to coexist rather than one replacing the other**. **② ⭐⭐⭐ It is generated from a CSV and says so** — the proposal states verbatim that a script renders the guide from a CSV data file **so that the published page stays in sync with the source data**, and the data file measurably carries seven columns: area, tool, URL, repository URL, language, whether the society hosts it, and a description ⭐⭐⭐ **Four things**: ⭐⭐⭐ **keeping the published page in sync with the source data is the line in this entry that best fits the round’s theme, the page being an artefact and the CSV the source**; ⭐⭐⭐ **one row per tool carrying the fields a reader needs to decide**, ⭐ **so the shape of the data determines what can be filtered**; ⭐⭐ **whether the society hosts a tool is a boolean field**, ⭐ **so hosting is a first-class dimension rather than something the reader must look up**; **and ⭐⭐ the twenty areas are measurably uneven**, reserving holding eight, simulation and synthetic claims six, credibility and experience rating five, frequency-severity pricing four, mortality and life contingencies four and data standards four, the rest one to three, ⭐ **so the list itself discloses the density of that ecosystem, reserving being densest while capital modelling holds one**. **③ ⭐⭐⭐ It makes language and hosting filterable** — the proposal states verbatim that the client-side script adds coloured language indicator dots **matching the interface’s own language colouring** and filter chips ⭐⭐ **Three things**: ⭐⭐ **the colours match the hosting platform’s linguist colours, so a reader learns no new colour scheme**; ⭐⭐ **filtering runs on the client, so a static page and a script need no server**, ⭐ **the same direction as the SQL macro library of an earlier round needing neither extension nor driver**; **and ⭐⭐ the two filter dimensions are language and hosting organisation**, ⭐ **the two most common ways of looking something up made directly interactive**. **④ ⭐⭐⭐ This entry used it as an external cross-check, which is both this round’s method and this entry’s added value** — comparing each of the sixty-three tools against the sources, titles and slugs of this site’s pool of 1,241 entries and wiki of 1,131 entries leaves **seventeen not found**, **most of them repositories the society itself hosts whose last push falls outside the window**, including a telematics simulation engine, a linear scoring package, an authoring template, a consumer vehicle toolkit, Stan models, a GLM package, a GAM examples repository, a GAN-based anonymisation study, a health-insurance fraud-detection project, a COVID-19 dataset, a presentation repository, an NLP catastrophe-loss project, a pull-request tutorial and an introduction to open source ⭐⭐⭐ **Three things**: ⭐⭐⭐ **the list therefore amounts to an externally sourced, checkable gap list, and this entry rates finding it as the most valuable methodological gain of the round, since reaching for a directory someone else compiled beats guessing more keywords**; ⭐⭐⭐ **the comparison also shows that the gap is not that nobody has built these things but that nobody pushed them inside the window**, ⭐ **so none was collected merely for existing, the list being recorded as a backlog to check instead**; **and ⭐⭐ this entry states plainly that the comparison was a rough string match on containment and slugified names**, ⚠️ **so the figure of seventeen may include things already held under different names, with no item-by-item manual review performed**. **⑤ ⭐ Other details**: **the proposal comes from an outside contributor**, ⭐ **so a professional body’s public directory can be filled in by someone outside it**; **its grouping of areas is a different cut from this site’s own categories**, ⚠️ **with no comparison made and no claim that either is better**; **and its text lists indexes and task views as a category of their own**, ⭐ **so other people’s indexes count as tools too**. **⑥ ⭐⭐ Readable with** [[cran-actuarial-task-view]], [[chainladder-python]], [[haute]], [[insurancerating]], [[lossmodels]] and [[reservingmodels]].

⚠️ **Stated plainly**: **① ⚠️⚠️ Unmerged and unlicensed**: the proposal is measurably open, **so it is not a published page of that society** and this entry records only a proposal and a data file, ⭐ **making no claim that it is live or adopted**; **and licence probes against both the target and the fork return 404 with no licence field**, ⚠️ **while the sixty-three tools it lists carry their own licences, which were not checked one by one**. **② ⚠️⚠️ Neither its page was opened nor any of its scripts run** — **the generator was not run, the static page and its script were not opened, and no check was run**; **so this entry does not claim the page renders, the filters work, or the generation behaves as described**, ⭐ **what it actually did being to read the data file row by row and to compare its sixty-three tools against the pool by string matching**. **③ ⚠️⚠️ Its inclusion criteria were not verified**, ⭐ **so what it leaves in or out, and whether anything obvious is missing, were not checked** — ⭐ **the single most important thing to verify next for this entry**. **④ ⭐ ⚠️ One counting discrepancy is recorded plainly**: **the proposal in the fork states verbatim fifty-eight tools across twenty functional areas while the proposal upstream states sixty-three listings under twenty headings**, **and this entry measured sixty-three tool rows**, ⭐ **so the fifty-eight is recorded as not matching measurement**, ⚠️ **possible explanations including a fork body not updated with the data or a different counting convention, with no judgement offered since the generator was not read**. **⑤ ⚠️ Whether the society will adopt it was not verified**, ⭐ **and this entry takes no position**. **⑥ ⚠️ This entry records what was seen on 2026-09-11**. **Verification note**: the target repository, its first pull request, the fork and the fork’s first pull request, and the organisation’s repository listing of forty-six repositories were all read via the GitHub API on 2026-09-11; **the field guide data file was read row by row over raw, measuring sixty-three tool rows across seven columns and twenty areas**; licence file probes against both roots returned 404; **nothing was cloned, no script was run, no page was opened, neither the licences nor the inclusion criteria of the listed tools were checked one by one, and no other network observation was made**.
